rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse and 19:64 and 21:27 establish that angels are protected from disobedience.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية دالة على عصمة الملائكة ونظيرها قوله : { وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By saying they descend by their Lord's permission, God indicates that angels do nothing without permission, as a husband requires permission for every outing.
rows.anchor: لم يقل : مأذونين بل قال : { بإذن ربهم } وهو إشارة إلى أنهم لا يتصرفون تصرفا ما إلا بإذنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God their Lord honors the angels and humbles sinners; Razi illustrates this with God's care for David and Abraham's guest, whom God had cared for.
rows.anchor: ربهم } يفيد تعظيما للملائكة وتحقيرا للعصاة

rows.speaker: داود
rows.claim: When dying, David asked God to be for Solomon as He had been for David; revelation answered that Solomon should be for God as David had been.
rows.anchor: روى أن داود لما مرض مرض الموت قال : إلهي كن لسليمان كما كنت لي

rows.speaker: إبراهيم الخليل
rows.claim: Abraham found a host whose host produced milk and honey by striking two stones; he wondered why he had not received such honor, and God replied that the host had belonged to Him, so He had cared for him.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم الخليل عليه السلام أنه فقد الضيف أياما فخرج بالسفرة ليلتمس ضيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means the angels descend because of every affair, with each angel assigned a different task.
rows.anchor: من أجل كل أمر ، والمعنى أن كل واحد منهم إنما نزل لمهم آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation assigns the angels many devotional and service tasks: bowing, prostration, prayer, reflection, teaching, conveying revelation, seeking the night's merit, or greeting believers.
rows.anchor: بعضهم للركوع وبعضهم للسجود ، وبعضهم بالدعاء

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most say angels descend because of each affair destined that year, good or bad; their descent is worship for people's welfare in religion, worldly life, and the hereafter.
rows.anchor: من أجل كل أمر قدر في تلك السنة من خير أو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading, من كل امرئ, means the angels descend for every person; a report says they greet every believing man and woman.
rows.anchor: قرأ بعضهم : { من كل * امرىء } أي من أجل كل إنسان ، وروى أنهم لا يلقون مؤمنا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: To reconcile mid-Sha'ban decrees with the Night of Power, a prophetic report says God determines destinies on the Night of Bara'a and hands them to their custodians on the Night of Power.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( إن الله يقدر المقادير في ليلة البراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reconciliation assigns lifespans and provisions to mid-Sha'ban, while the Night of Power determines beneficial, blessed, and safe affairs.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يقدر ليلة البراءة الآجال والأرزاق / وليلة القدر يقدر الأمور التي فيها الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view assigns to the Night of Power affairs that honor the religion and benefit Muslims, while mid-Sha'ban records those who will die for the Angel of Death.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يقدر في ليلة القدر ما يتعلق به إعزاز الدين ، وما فيه النفع العظيم للمسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the night is peace because angels descend in successive groups from the start of night until dawn, repeatedly greeting the obedient.
rows.anchor: أن ليلة القدر ، إلى طلوع الفجر سلام أي تسلم الملائكة على المطيعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the greetings should not be slighted: seven angels' greeting brought Abraham greater joy than worldly kingship, and their greeting made Nimrod's fire cool; this night brings that honor to Muhammad's community, whose hearts should be offered sincerely.
rows.anchor: سبعة من الملائكة سلموا على الخليل في قصة العجل الحنيذ ، فازداد فرحع بذلك على فرحع بملك الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A view takes salām as safety from evils and afflictions: only good, benefit, and well-being descend that night, unlike ordinary nights whose hours have differing preferred acts.
rows.anchor: أنه سلام من الشرور والآفات ، أي سلامة وهذا كما يقال

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says the night is free of wind, harm, thunderbolts, and similar disturbances.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : سلام أي الليلة سالمة عن الرياح والأذى والصواعق إلى ما شابه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says Satan cannot commit evil during the night.
rows.anchor: سلام لا يستطيع الشيطان فيها سوءا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposed pause after من كل أمر connects salām to the previous phrase, so destined goodness and safety last until dawn; Razi calls this reading weak.
rows.anchor: أن الوقف عند قوله : { من كل أمر * سلام } فيتصل السلام بما قبله ومعناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says every portion from nightfall to dawn is equally better for worship than a thousand months, unlike other nights with preferred hours for prayer or supplication.
rows.anchor: من أولها إلى مطلع الفجر سالمة في أن العبادة في كل واحد من أجزائها خير من ألف شهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final interpretation takes salām as a garden or paradise, since Dār al-Salām is one of Paradise's names.
rows.anchor: سلام هي ، أي جنة هي لأن من أسماء الجنة دار السلام

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says kasra in maṭlaʿ names the time of rising, or possibly its place; the time sense fits this verse.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ بكسر اللام فهو اسم لوقت الطلوع وكذا مكان الطلوع مطلع قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والفراء
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda, al-Farrāʾ, and others prefer fatḥa because maṭlaʿ is a verbal noun; a place-name makes no sense here.
rows.anchor: أما أبو عبيدة والفراء وغيرهما فإنهم اختاروا فتح اللام لأنه بمعنى المصدر

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī allows the kasra form to be a verbal noun, citing source patterns normally expected with fatḥa but occasionally pronounced with kasra, as in المكبر and المعجز.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي : ويمكن حمله على المصدر أيضا ، لأن من المصادر التي ينبغي أن تكون على المفعل

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's explanation, preferred by Razi, resolves the apparent contradiction: verse 98:1 reports disbelievers saying they would leave their religion only when the promised Prophet came, while 98:4 reports that his arrival actually divided them from truth.
rows.anchor: الوجه الذي لخصه صاحب الكشاف

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī removes the conflict by reading the sense as they would not abandon disbelief even when the proof came; Razi rejects this because حتى does not mean that in Arabic.
rows.anchor: هكذا ذكره القاضي إلا أن تفسير لفظة حتى بهذا ليس من اللغة في شيء

rows.speaker: ابن عرفة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿArafa reads انفكاك as ceasing to praise Muhammad: before his coming they mentioned his virtues, but after he came they split into hostile claims; the imperfect can carry past meaning, as in 2:102 and 2:89.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عرفة : أي حتى أتتهم ، فاللفظ لفظ المضارع ومعناه الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says the whole group remained in disbelief until the Messenger came; afterward the group changed because some believed and others remained disbelievers, satisfying حتى.
rows.anchor: كفى ذلك في العمل بمدلول لفظ حتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view says they were previously certain of their inherited religions, but Muhammad's coming unsettled their convictions and left them doubtful about their own and other religions; Razi compares this to humanity before prophetic missions.
rows.anchor: كانوا قبل مبعث الرسول منفكين عن التردد في كفرهم بل كانوا جازمين به معتقدين حقيقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers comprise two groups: scriptural communities, including Jews and Christians who altered their religion and scripture, and polytheists with no scripture.
rows.anchor: الكفار كانوا جنسين أحدهما : أهل الكتاب كفرق اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To explain من, one view takes it as explanatory, like the phrase about avoiding the abomination of idols in 22:30.
rows.anchor: كلمة من ههنا ليست للتبعيض بل للتبيين كقوله : { فاجتنبوا الرجس من الاوثان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says those rejecting Muhammad include some People of the Book: Christians' trinitarianism and Jews' anthropomorphism are forms of shirk; several coordinated descriptions can name one group, as in 9:112.
rows.anchor: بعضهم من أهل الكتاب ، وذلك لأن النصارى مثلثة واليهود عامتهم مشبهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars include Zoroastrians among scriptural communities, citing a prophetic instruction to treat them by the People of the Book's rule; others exclude them because the verse concerns Arabian Jews and Christians, as in 6:156.
rows.anchor: ذكر بعض العلماء أنهم داخلون في أهل الكتاب لقوله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though واو gives no sequence, People of the Book come first because the surah is Medinan, they knew scripture and could best recognize Muhammad, their persistence was more blameworthy, and others followed their example.
rows.anchor: أن السورة مدنية فكأن أهل الكتاب هم المقصودون بالذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them People of the Book rather than Jews and Christians highlights their learning, which can honor them or intensify their culpability and punishment for disbelief.
rows.anchor: لأن كونه عالما يقتضي مزيد قبح في كفره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some jurists infer that all disbelief is one religion, so a polytheist may inherit from a Jew and vice versa, because the verse places both under disbelief.
rows.anchor: قال العلماء : الكفر كله ملة واحدة ، فالمشرك يرث اليهودي وبالعكس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others infer from the conjunction that the categories differ: a protected scripturalist is not a polytheist, consistent with the reported distinction concerning marriage and slaughtered food.
rows.anchor: أن العطف أوجب المغايرة ، فلذلك نقول : الذمي ليس بمشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming People of the Book warns against trusting learned people, since Quran scholars can repeat the failures of earlier communities.
rows.anchor: نبه بذكر أهل الكتاب أنه لا يجوز الاغترار بأهل العلم إذ قد حدث في أهل القرآن مثل ما حدث

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl derives انفكاك from opening or removing a bond: release follows close attachment; thus disbelievers clung strongly to their religion until the evident proof came, and bayyina is proof separating truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: الانفكاك هو انفراج الشيء عن الشيء وأصله من الفك وهو الفتح والزوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those identifying the proof as Muhammad say his extraordinary seriousness in proclaiming prophethood rules out fabrication and mental deficiency, while the totality of his qualities reaches miraculous perfection, as al-Jāḥiẓ and al-Ghazālī argued.
rows.anchor: أن ذاته كانت بينة على نبوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further argument is that Muhammad's numerous, manifest miracles make him himself a proof; God accordingly calls him a shining lamp in 33:46.
rows.anchor: أن معجزاته عليه الصلاة والسلام كانت في غاية الظهور وكانت أيضا في غاية الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next phrase رسول من الله is grammatically taken as an appositive to البينة; ʿAbd Allāh reads رسولا as a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: فهو رفع على البدن من البينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in البينة identifies the Prophet foretold in the Torah and Gospel, or magnifies him as the ultimate proof; the indefinite رسول then adds emphasis by naming him as a messenger of exceptional stature.
rows.anchor: والألف واللام في قوله : { البينة } للتعريف أي هو الذي سبق ذكره

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim says the proof means messengers from God who recite purified sheets, as in the request for a heavenly book and for unfolded pages.
rows.anchor: وهو قول أبي مسلم قال : المراد من قوله : / { حتى تأتيهم البينة }

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
rows.claim: Qatāda and Ibn Zayd take the proof as the Quran, citing 20:133; رسول من الله then has an omitted noun, meaning that proof is revelation and the Messenger recites purified sheets.
rows.anchor: القول الثالث : وهو قتادة وابن زيد : { البينة } هي القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣuḥuf means sheets that contain writing; the adjective purified formally modifies the sheets but really describes the Quran they contain.
rows.anchor: الصحف جمع صحيفة وهي ظرف للمكتوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes the purified sheets as exalted and protected from falsehood, like the Quran's immunity from falsehood in 41:42.
rows.anchor: مرفوعة مطهرة } عن الباطل وهي كقوله : { لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading says the Quran is purified of blameworthy mention because it receives the finest praise.
rows.anchor: مطهرة عن الذكر القبيح فإن القرآن يذكر بأحسن الذكر ويثني عليه أحسن الثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading says only the ritually pure should touch the sheets, as in 56:79.
rows.anchor: أي ينبغي أن لا يمسها إلا المطهرون ، كقوله تعالى : { فى كتاب مكنون * لا يمسه إلا المطهرون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كتب can mean the written verses in the sheets, or rulings, as صاحب النظم argues from كتب الله لأغلبن and the hadith invoking God's Book as His judgment.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب النظم : الكتب قد يكون بمعنى الحكم : { كتب الله لاغلبن }

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains qayyima as upright, without deviation, and as clarifying truth from falsehood; the root conveys standing or being established.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : مستقيمة لا عوج فيها تبين الحق من الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation makes qayyima mean established and independently standing as proof, from the idiom of carrying through a matter.
rows.anchor: أن تكون القيمة بمعنى القائمة أي هي قائمة مستقلة بالحجة والدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Muhammad was unlettered, reciting what is written in the sheets counts as reciting their contents; a book attributed to Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq says he could read but not write, perhaps miraculously.
rows.anchor: إذا تلا مثلا المسطور في تلك الصحف كان تاليا ما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse names only the People of the Book because polytheists were not left on their religion: converts were accepted and those persisting were killed, unlike scripturalists who could remain under jizya; they also knew Muhammad's prophethood from scripture.
rows.anchor: أن المشركين لم يقروا على دينهم فمن آمن فهو المراد ومن لم يؤمن قتل ، بخلاف أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says the verse refutes predestinarians: people did not divide into misery and felicity in their fathers' loins before proof came.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي : هذه الآية تبطل قول القدرية الذين قالوا : إن الناس تفرقوا في الشقاوة والسعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls al-Jubbāʾī's argument weak: God's knowledge and will are eternal, but their manifestation in accountable people occurs only after the relevant condition.
rows.anchor: المراد منه أن علم الله بذلك وإرادته له حاصل في الأزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The timing after the proof attributes division and disbelief to the people themselves, while guidance and success are attributed to God.
rows.anchor: الخير والتوفيق مضاف إلى الله ، والشر والتفرق والكفر مضاف إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse consoles Muhammad: their division reflects stubbornness, not deficient evidence, and repeats an old pattern among their ancestors after the Sabbath and calf proofs.
rows.anchor: المقصود من هذه الآية تسلية الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم أي لا يغمنك تفرقهم فليس ذلك لقصور في الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command may repeat what Jews and Christians received in the Torah and Gospel, which would also bind Muslims; Razi prefers that Muhammad commanded these duties anew because it gives the verse new legal force, follows the prior mention of Muhammad, and declares this religion straight. The latter is attributed to Muqātil.
rows.anchor: وما أمر أهل الكتاب على لسان محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا بهذه الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose-lām cannot mean God acts to gain an end: that would imply need, regress, incapacity, or purposelessness, all impossible for God.
rows.anchor: لا يمكن حمله على ظاهره فلا بد فيه من التأويل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says Arabic often uses lām where أن is intended in desire or command; reading عبد الله has أن, so the meaning is simply that they were commanded to worship sincerely. This supports requiring intention in every commanded act, including wudu when combined with 5:6.
rows.anchor: العرب تجعل اللام في موضع أن في الأمر والإرادة كثيرا

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila affirm divine acts and rulings have purposes, read the lām literally, and infer that every commanded act is for worship and requires intention; Razi says their argument is strong, apart from prior contemplation of God, where rational proof limits the generality.
rows.anchor: وأما المعتزلة فإنهم يوجبون تعليل أفعال الله وأحكامه بالأغراض ، لا جرم أجروا الآية على ظاهرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unexpressed agent in أمروا softens the command: since worship is difficult, God intimates it like a mother requesting cupping, easing the offense of refusal; the wording also evokes God's self-imposed mercy.
rows.anchor: العبادة شاقة ولا أريد مشقتك إرادة أصلية بل إرادتي لعبادتك كإرادة الوالدة لحجامتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the view that moral good and evil are rationally knowable, reason also commands worship because gratitude to the giver of immense blessings is intellectually obligatory.
rows.anchor: لست أنا الآمر للعبادة فقط ، بل عقلك أيضا يأمرك

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: Worship is owed because the servant is God's servant and God is Lord, not to obtain Paradise or avoid Hell; worship motivated by reward or punishment makes those benefits the real object and God merely a means.
rows.anchor: بل لأجل أنك عبد وهو رب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is humility, not merely obedience in ordinary speech; in religious usage it is commanded obedience joined with utmost reverence, due only to the unique God. It requires both knowledge of God's greatness and divine command, absent respectively in a child's prayer and a Jew's act.
rows.anchor: العبادة هي التذلل ، ومنه طريق معبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincerity means acting from one motive alone, with no other motive influencing the act.
rows.anchor: الإخلاص هو أن يأتي بالفعل خالصا لداعية واحدة ، ولا يكون لغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A homily says God asks only a portion of one's capacity, such as one sheep from forty, but requires doing that portion only for Him; an itch or throat-clearing during prayer serves oneself, while distracting attention serves Satan.
rows.anchor: ما بذلت كل مقدوري لك حتى أطلب منك كل مقدورك ، بل بذلت لك البعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God and sound reason will the same wise good; since God created the earth for people, they should dedicate all their acts to Him.
rows.anchor: لا تريد إلا ما أريد ولا أريد إلا ما تريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukhliṣīn is a circumstantial phrase showing sincerity must continue from start to finish: act for God's sake, not display, reputation, or another goal, and do not make Paradise or escape from Hell one's motive.
rows.anchor: قوله : { مخلصين } نصب على الحال فهو تنبيه على ما يجب من تحصيل الإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Torah saying promises that a small deed done for God's face is much, while a large deed done for another's sake is little.
rows.anchor: وفي التوراة : ما آريد به وجهي فقليله كثير وما أريد به غير وجهي فكثيره قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mixing worship with a second motive compromises sincerity: an extra sacrifice for a ruler or public show of humility is shirk, and giving zakat to parents, children, or dependents to please them fails the purity of motive.
rows.anchor: مثل الواجب من الأضحية شاة ، فإذا ذبحت إثنتين واحدة لله وواحدة للأمير

rows.speaker: السلف
rows.claim: Some early authorities gloss mukhliṣīn as acknowledging God alone in worship.
rows.anchor: اختلفت ألفاظ السلف في معنى قوله : { مخلصين } قال بعضهم : مقرين له بالعبادة

rows.speaker: السلف
rows.claim: Other early authorities gloss it as sincerely intending God's pleasure in worship.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : قاصدين بقلوبهم رضا الله في العبادة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains sincerity as worshipping God as one, without associating anything with Him, supported by 9:31.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : أي يعبدونه موحدين له لا يعبدون معه غيره

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets ḥunafāʾ as following Abraham's religion, with 16:123 and 60:4 as exemplars; since people naturally imitate, one should imitate Abraham's renunciation of idols and total surrender.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : متبعين دين إبراهيم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi exhorts imitation of Abraham, who surrendered himself to fire, gave wealth to guests, and offered his son, thereby abandoning self, property, and child for God.
rows.anchor: تبرأ من الأصنام وهذا غير عجيب فإنه قد تبرأ من نفسه حين سلمها إلى النيران

rows.speaker: إبراهيم الخليل
rows.claim: In a devotional anecdote, Abraham hears the praise سبحان قدوس, asks it to be repeated, and says he will not repeat it without payment; Gabriel reveals God spoke, Abraham gives all he owns, then refuses attachment even to Gabriel.
rows.anchor: بل روى أنه سمع سبوح قدوس فاستطابه ، ولم ير شخصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If one cannot imitate Abraham, Razi urges following his young son, who submitted to God's command of sacrifice despite his youth.
rows.anchor: فإن لم تقدر على متابعة إبراهيم ، فاجتهد في متابعة ولده الصبي

rows.speaker: هاجر
rows.claim: Razi also urges following Hajar: when Abraham left her alone in Mecca without water or provisions, she accepted and endured the ordeal once he signaled that God had commanded it.
rows.anchor: قالت آلله أمرك بهذا ؟ فأومأ برأسه نعم ، فرضيت بذلك وصبرت على تلك المشاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes ḥunafāʾ as upright; a person with a bent foot is called aḥnaf optimistically, as a blind person may be called seeing, with parallels in 41:30 and 1:6.
rows.anchor: المراد من قوله : { حنفاء } أي مستقيمين والحنف هو الاستقامة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the word means pilgrims; Hajj is mentioned before prayer because it includes prayer and expenditure.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما حجاجا ، وذلك لأنه ذكر العباد أولا

rows.speaker: أبو قلابة
rows.claim: Abū Qilāba says a ḥanīf believes in every messenger without exception; denying the greatest Prophet is incompatible with true ḥanīfism.
rows.anchor: قال أبو قلابة / الحنيف الذي آمن بجميع الرسل ولم يستثن أحدا منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes ḥanīfism as the whole religion, supported by the prophetic description of the easy, tolerant ḥanīfiyya.
rows.anchor: حنفاء أي جامعين لكل الدين إذ الحنيفية كل الدين ، قال عليه السلام : ( بعثن بالحنيفية السهلة السمحة )

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda interprets ḥunafāʾ as circumcised and abstaining from marriage to close relatives; it first negates prohibited conduct, then affirms prayer.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : هي الختان وتحريم نكاح المحارم أي مختونين محرمين لنكاح الأم والمحارم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim derives ḥanīf from the physical deviation of the big toe and says the ḥanīf turns away from other religions toward Islam.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : أصله من الحنف في الرجل ، وهو إدبار إبهامها عن أخوانها

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas says the ḥanīf faces the qibla in prayer, echoing the prayer's declaration of turning one's face to the Creator.
rows.anchor: قال الربيع بن أنيس : الحنيف الذي يستقبل القبلة بصلاته

rows.speaker: المبرد والزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjāj supply an omitted noun: this is the upright or established community's religion; al-Farrāʾ instead calls it an adjective-noun genitive construction with an emphatic tāʾ.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد والزجاج : ذلك دين الملة القيمة ، فالقيمة نعت لموصوف محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True religion combines sound foundations and practice: Jews, Christians, and Magians may exert themselves without true belief, while Murjiʾites neglect works; sincerity and belief join prayer and zakat in one balanced religion.
rows.anchor: الكمال في كل شيء إنما يحصل إذا حصل الأصل والفرع معا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi analogizes the components to a body: belief is its heart, prayer its face, and zakat its expressive tongue; this whole straight religion serves people's present and future welfare, as in 6:161 and 18:2.
rows.anchor: قلب دينك الاعتقاد ووجهه الصلاة ولسانه الواصف لحقيقته الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may honor believers because they imitate divine kindness through charity, while angels offer devotion; at judgment angels will marvel that believers practiced both, fulfilling the greeting in 39:73.
rows.anchor: أقاموا الصلاة أتوا بالعبودية وآتوا الزكاة أتوا بالإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer resembles knowledge and zakat resembles capacity: knowledge without power is crippled and power without knowledge is mad, but together they make a complete soul and upright religion.
rows.anchor: فكذا الصلاة للذين كالعلم والزكاة كالقدرة ، فإذا اجتمعتا سمي الدين قيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence eases people in: begin with belief and sincerity, then prayer, then the harder duty of charity, whose timing is softened by the rule that zakat is not due until wealth has completed a year.
rows.anchor: أمر رسوله أن يدعوهم إلى أسهل شيء ، وهو القول والاعتقاد فقال : { مخلصين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who define faith as utterance, belief, and deed argue that the verse names all three and calls the whole the upright religion; since religion is Islam and Islam is accepted faith, faith must include all three, refuting definitions as knowledge, profession, or both alone.
rows.anchor: مجموع القول والفعل والعمل هو الدين والدين هو الإسلام والإسلام هو الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that وذلك could point only to sincerity, requiring no omitted words, and even if it points to the whole list, it names the complete upright religion and its results, not faith's minimum essence; thus the inference does not settle the dispute.
rows.anchor: لم لا يجوز أن تكون الإشارة بقوله : { وذلك } إلى الإخلاص فقط ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah first mentions disbelievers, then the commanded way of believers, and closes by restating both groups, beginning again with the disbelievers and their lasting punishment and status as worst creation.
rows.anchor: أعاد في آخر هذه السورة ذكر كلا الفريقين ، فبدأ أيضا بحال الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of the Book precede polytheists because the Prophet prioritized God's right over his own: he prayed for guidance after his tooth was broken but invoked punishment when prayer was missed at the Trench; God then gives precedence to those who injured Muhammad, the People of the Book, over those who insulted God, the polytheists.
rows.anchor: كان يقدم حق الله سبحانه على حق نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reason is that People of the Book's offense was graver: unlike nearby polytheists, they knew from scripture that Muhammad would come yet rejected him knowingly.
rows.anchor: أما أهل الكتاب فقد كانوا يستفتحون برسالته ويقرون بمبعثه فلما جاءهم أنكروه مع العلم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using the verb كفروا for People of the Book implies they were not disbelievers from the beginning but rejected the Torah, Gospel, and Muhammad after his mission; المشركين as a noun characterizes polytheists raised on idols and denial of resurrection.
rows.anchor: تنبيها على أن أهل الكتاب ما كانوا كافرين من أول الأمر لأنهم كانوا مصدقين بالتوراة والإنجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although scripturalists and polytheists differ in what they deny, sharing punishment does not erase different degrees within Hell; those who sought elevation end up at its deepest low.
rows.anchor: وإن اشتراكا في ذلك لكنه لا ينافي اشتراكهم في هذا القدر تفاوتهم في مراتب العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their offense is especially grave because they disbelieved despite God's great beneficence; wrongdoing to a benefactor is worse, and punishment scales with the crime, from reprimand and legal penalties up to retaliation and death for contempt toward the Messenger.
rows.anchor: فكان إحسان الله إلى هؤلاء الكفار أعظم أنواع الإحسان وإساءتهم وكفرهم أقبح أنواع الإساءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is deep, dark, terrifying, and inescapable; its inmates remain forever, with no one to pity them, and are condemned as the worst creatures.
rows.anchor: استحقوا أعظم العقوبات ، وهو نار جهنم ، فإنها نار في موضع عميق مظلم هائل لا مفر عنه البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi gives three reasons Hell lacks أبدا here though Paradise includes it: mercy exceeds wrath, punishments and expiations can overlap while rewards do not, and a divine saying to David directs people to God's vast mercy.
rows.anchor: التنبيه على أن رحمته أزيد من غضبه

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads البرية with hamza; the others omit it. Although hamza reflects the etymological root برأ, common usage drops it as in النبي and الذرية, and Nāfiʿ's reading refutes derivation from soil.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع البريئة بالهمز ، وقرأ الباقون بغير همز وهو من برأ الله الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them the worst creation excludes others: they are worse than thieves who stole Muhammad's description from scripture, bandits who block truth, and ignorant people, since learned arrogance is stubborn disbelief; evil scholars face the severest threat.
rows.anchor: شر من السراق ، لأنهم سرقوا من كتاب الله ، صفة محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat is not universal: those who repent and embrace Islam leave it; one view also excludes earlier disbelievers such as Pharaoh, while the promise to believers applies to earlier and later people as the best community.
rows.anchor: لا بل هي مخصوصة بصورتين إحداهما : أن من تاب منهم وأسلم خرج عن الوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Threat before promise is like medicine before food: purification by warning prepares one to benefit from reward, as Hippocrates teaches; hardship turns people toward God, whereas safety makes them turn away, as in 29:65.
rows.anchor: الوعيد كالدواء ، والوعد كالغذاء ، ويجب تقديم الدواء حتى إذا صار البدن نقيا انتفع بالغذاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ending with promise is glad tidings: after God brought a person from an impure place into the world purified, He will bring that person pure into Paradise.
rows.anchor: لما لم يكن بد من الأمرين ختمت بالوعد الذي هو بشارة مني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who say righteous deeds are outside the definition of faith cite the conjunction and argue that what is joined by واو differs from what precedes it.
rows.anchor: احتج من قال : إن الطاعات ليست داخلة في مسمى الإيمان بأن الأعمال الصالحة معطوفة في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording الذين آمنوا, rather than المؤمنين, honors those who sustained Islam when it was weak and gave wealth and lives, like those distinguished for spending before victory in 57:10.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أنهم أقاموا سوق الإسلام حال كساده ، وبذلوا الأموال والمهج لأجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who require dying in faith for final salvation argue that one sincere act of faith receives this reward, while someone dying in disbelief does not; therefore such a person never truly attained faith before death.
rows.anchor: الذين يعتبرون الموافاة يحتجون بهذه الآية ، وذلك لأنها تدل على أن من أتى بالإيمان مرة واحدة فله هذا الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural-to-plural relation in عملوا الصالحات means each person need not perform every righteous deed: each has a fitting share, such as giving for the rich and receiving for the poor.
rows.anchor: من مقابلة الجمع بالجمع ، فلا يكلف الواحد بجميع الصالحات ، بل لكل مكلف حظ

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet saying a believer's rank with God on Judgment Day exceeds the angels' rank, and he cited 98:7 as proof.
rows.anchor: روى أبو هريرة أنه عليه السلام قال : ( أتعجبون من منزلة الملائكة من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: يزيد النحوي
rows.claim: Yazīd al-Naḥwī says barīya means the children of Adam, from soil, so the word itself cannot include angels; Razi offers this as one reason the superiority argument is weak.
rows.anchor: ما روى عن يزيد النحوي أن البرية بنو آدم من البرا وهو التراب فلا يدخل الملك فيه البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the verse is not restricted to humans and may include angels; other evidence, rather than this wording, is needed to exclude them.
rows.anchor: غير مختص بالبشر بل يدخل فيه الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arguments favoring angels cite their creation from light, higher dwelling, role in provision and souls, greater knowledge, freedom from petty sins, and uninterrupted glorification day and night, unlike humans preoccupied with appetite.
rows.anchor: الفضيلة إما مكتسبة أو موهوبة ، فإن نظرت إلى الموهوبة فأصلهم من نور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion of whether humans or angels are superior continues in the earlier commentary on al-Baqara; the segment then supplies only the text of 98:8.
rows.anchor: وتمام القول في هذه المسألة قد تقدم في سورة البقرة
